summary: A 115-foot concrete tower on a cliff-edged point in Mendocino County, rebuilt in 1908 after the 1906 earthquake wrecked the brick tower of 1870.

lens.where: fog signal building (moved 2008, per Lighthouse Friends)

access.note: Run by Point Arena Lighthouse Keepers, Inc.; store, museums and tower tours (check hours).

stay.note: Keepers' houses are rented as vacation homes (per the owner's website).

events.note: Whistle first sounded 25 Nov 1871 per Lighthouse Friends; NRHP dates fog signal station to 1870
New fog-signal house completed August 1896, 125 ft back from the eroding old site
Steamer San Benito wrecked 22 Nov 1896; keeper Brown's rescue attempt
Telephone line to the town of Point Arena established November 1898
Keeper Jefferson M. Brown awarded Life-Saving gold medal 17 Oct 1899
Earthquake of 18 April 1906 wrecked the brick tower and lens
Temporary wooden tower with the old lantern lit 5 Jan 1907
Reinforced concrete tower, first of its type in California
New tower lit 15 Sept 1908 with a first-order Fresnel lens
Fog signal changed from air siren to air diaphone
Automated beacon placed on tower balcony June 1977; Fresnel lens retired
Point Arena Lighthouse Keepers, Inc. leased the station

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP calls the fog signal station (1870) the oldest building; Lighthouse Friends gives a 1871 appropriation and 25 Nov 1871 start; the Light-House Board reports show the present building was completed August 1896 after the old site eroded. USLHS also gives fog_signal_year 1896 for the building.

notes_for_editor: Construction of the 1870 tower rests on Lighthouse Friends (which quotes the 1869 Light-House Board report) because the 1869-1870 reports are not in the local corpus; worth replacing with the primary report. The 1906 keeper's log quotation is second-hand via Lighthouse Digest (Lighthouse Friends prints the same text). Lighthouse Friends describes two attempts by Keeper Brown at the San Benito and an abandoned third; the Life-Saving Service list says three; the story states the disagreement. Miller and Poznanovich rows in the LSS medal list were matched by position (they follow Brown's row with 'do' marks), please check the page image. Keeper roster built mechanically from roster.py (USLHS); Owens is listed there from 1937 (second assistant), matching Lighthouse Friends. Admiral/efficiency flag rests on the Bulletin 1924-29 index only. Lighthouse Friends gives 1895 for the new fog signal building; the Board's reports say contract work in the 1896 report and completion August 1896. Newspaper searches (Chronicling America) returned nothing usable. The pointarenalighthouse.com current site returned HTTP 429; the old-site history page was used for ownership, hours and automation. Coast Guard crew names from 1948 on are from the USLHS roster only.
